title: Keystone Shortflow Compiler: transcript-to-shortflow adaptor for safe ops micro-actions
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build 'Keystone': a compiler service that converts incident transcripts, support chat snippets, and canonical runbook fragments into typed, idempotent 'shortflows' — minimal task units that can be executed by the admin runtime. Goal is safer, auditable automated remediations that are replayable (dry-run), permission-checked, and instrumented for cost/latency. This bridges support automation (quickfixes) with the runbooks-as-tasks model while retaining human-in-the-loop approvals for high-risk operations.
acceptance_criteria: Keystone accepts a transcript+context bundle and returns a validated shortflow JSON schema (v1) with step types, param typing, and optional recovery branches.
Runtime executes shortflows in dry-run mode with deterministic simulated outcomes and produces a replayable trace that maps to original transcript tokens.
All generated shortflows pass RBAC gates and an autosafety policy that rejects non-idempotent or destructive operations unless explicitly allowed by an approver.
End-to-end test coverage covering common failure modes (timeouts, partial failures, ambiguous intents) with snapshots for regression testing.
Telemetry: per-shortflow tokenization length, compile latency, rejection reason, and success/failure rate visible on Ops Dashboard.
implementation_notes: Compiler staged pipeline: (1) Intent extraction (LLM classifier), (2) Step synthesis (template-backed generator), (3) Type-check and idempotency analyzer, (4) Safety policy evaluation, (5) Shortflow emit and provenance metadata tagging.
Prefer open LLM models in the curated catalog for offline compatibility; provide a model-agnostic interface so Dedicated/Private deployments can swap model backends.
Use existing KV cache helpers for prefix extraction where transcripts repeat across incidents to reduce compile cost.
Shortflow schema v1 fields: idempotency_key, steps[{action, args, precondition, compensation}], provenance{transcript_id, cue_tokens, model_version}, entropy_score, safety_flags.
Persist compiled shortflows to an append-only store with immutability tags for audit.
design_decisions: Decision: Keep shortflows declarative (no arbitrary code) to simplify static analysis and sandboxing.
Decision: Two-mode output: 'suggested' (for human review) and 'executable' (passes safety policy) to enable gradual automation rollouts.
Decision: Leverage existing admin-runtime step types rather than inventing new primitives — reduces surface area for RBAC and telemetry.
Trade-off: Initial compiler will be conservative and produce smaller atomic steps to avoid risky compound actions; may increase number of steps per incident.
Decision: All shortflows include a 'replay_seed' and mapping to transcript indices for deterministic simulation in dry-run.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: LLM hallucination can synthesize unsafe commands. Mitigation: strict safety-policy blacklist and conservative confidence thresholds; fallback to human review on low confidence.
Risk: Overfitting templates may miss edge-case repairs. Mitigation: add telemetry for 'unknown' intents and provide a feedback loop to expand templates from annotated incidents.
Risk: Permission escalation if compiled steps bypass RBAC. Mitigation: enforce runtime RBAC checks and require approver signatures for steps touching privileged resources.
Risk: Increased compile cost on spikes. Mitigation: batch compile requests and rate-limit per-customer; provide warm caches for frequent transcripts.
telemetry_and_alerting: Alert: >1% of compiles resulting in 'safety_block' for a given customer -> paging to SRE for policy tuning
Dashboard: Ops Shortflows overview with heatmap of intents vs. rejection reasons and median replay simulation time
qa_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and idempotency analyzer.
Golden-file integration tests for 50 canonical transcripts (saved under testdata/keystone).
Chaos test: random partial step failures and verify that compensation branches are emitted and that dry-run trace matches expectation.
Manual review sessions: 3 iterations with Support engineers annotating suggested shortflows for precision/recall measurements.
Staged canary deploy to Dedicated then hosted, with telemetry gating before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiment): internal-only UI for support agents to generate suggested shortflows (no exec). Collect feedback for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (canary): enable executable shortflows for low-risk namespaces with dry-run enforcement and opt-in automation. Monitor metrics for 7 days.
Phase 2 (gradual): increase namespaces and allow limited auto-execute for curated shortflows under watch. Introduce auto-rollback hooks.
Phase 3 (GA): expose Shortflow compiler via Console UI and API, add audit export and compliance reporting.
Rollback: disable automation flag and invalidate unexecuted shortflows; runtime will continue honoring immutability for already-executed traces.
